summary:
Mission Architect is a browser-based space mission design game. Players assemble a spacecraft by choosing a launch vehicle, an orbit or trajectory, a power source and science instruments, all under hard limits on budget, payload mass, power and data downlink. They then run a simulation that explains in plain language exactly why the mission succeeded or failed, and what design change would fix it.

It addresses the Space Mission Design Game challenge with three scored missions (Orbital Survey, Lunar Landing, Asteroid Rendezvous) and a sandbox mode. It adds three difficulty levels, random events and unexpected constraints, live 3D spacecraft and trajectory viewers, and a resource-consumption dashboard. Players also get leaderboards, mission reports, and designs they can save, share and compare. Teams of up to four can play cooperatively with specialist roles, or compete head-to-head on the same objective.

It matters because real mission design is a series of trade-offs. The game teaches that reasoning, and each figure is labeled with the NASA source it is modeled on.
details:
What it does- The player picks a mission, then designs a spacecraft: launch vehicle, orbit or trajectory, power source (solar, RTG or battery) and up to two instruments. Four live meters (payload mass, power, budget, downlink) update as choices change, along with a projected science score. Options that would break a limit are disabled, with a tooltip explaining which constraint they violate. On launch, a flight-readiness review checks each constraint, and the verdict names the exact failure and the specific fix.

Modes--> Solo, Co-op (up to four players with Flight Director, Spacecraft Engineer, Science Lead and Comms Officer roles, each owning a subsystem and needing to vote GO), and Versus (2–4 teams designing against the same mission, ranked on a scoreboard). Sandbox removes all constraints.

Depth- Three difficulty levels, ten random flight events, unexpected launch-review constraints, a telemetry playback dashboard (power, data, spend, propellant), post-mission analysis with a “best feasible design” reveal, rankings, saved designs with side-by-side comparison, and shareable design codes.

Built with- React, TypeScript, three.js (react-three-fiber), Framer Motion and Vite, deployed on Vercel.

Impact- It lets students experience real mission trade-offs (mass versus power versus downlink versus cost) without needing an engineering background.

Site- https://mission-architect-iota.vercel.app/
